title: Form Analytics
content: Build form analytics tracking. Field focus: track which fields get focus. Time spent: measure time on each field. Errors: track validation errors encountered. Submission: track successful vs abandoned. Field changes: detect frequently changed fields. Drop-off: identify where users abandon form. Heatmap: optional visual representation of interactions.

variants.detailed: Build form analytics tracking. Field focus: track which fields get focus. Time spent: measure time on each field. Errors: track validation errors encountered. Submission: track successful vs abandoned. Field changes: detect frequently changed fields. Drop-off: identify where users abandon form. Heatmap: optional visual representation of interactions.
variants.advanced: Build comprehensive form analytics for optimization insights. Tracking events: field focus, field blur, value change, validation error, step navigation, submission attempt, successful submission, abandonment. Field-level metrics: focus count, time spent (first focus to blur), error occurrences per field, change count (how often user modifies). Form-level metrics: total time to complete, submission success rate, abandonment rate, abandonment point (which field/step). Funnel analysis: for multi-step forms, conversion rate per step, step abandonment rates. Error analysis: which fields cause most errors, error messages shown, error resolution success. Event format: {event, field, timestamp, value (hashed if sensitive), sessionId, formId}. Privacy: never track actual values of sensitive fields (passwords, SSN), hash or omit. Implementation: useEffect hooks on field events, context for form-wide tracking. Data collection: batch events, send periodically or on navigation, beacon API for abandonment. Storage backend: send to analytics service (Segment, Amplitude, custom), or local collection endpoint. Visualization: dashboard showing funnel, field performance, error rates, time distribution. Heatmap: visual overlay showing click/focus density on form. A/B testing: track variant identifier for form experiments. Sampling: for high-traffic forms, sample percentage of sessions. User identification: anonymous session ID, or user ID if authenticated. Alerts: notify on unusual abandonment rates or error spikes. Recommendations: surface fields needing improvement based on data.
